title: Rollover MVC - unstable pelvis
objectives: Recognize hemorrhagic shock from pelvic fx (HR > SBP)
Pelvic binder; scoop instead of log-roll
Scene time < 10 min; early TRAUMA ALERT
Destination: UVMMC Level 1 by ground (<= 60 min, 4.9); recognize air is not faster
Permissive fluids in 250 mL boluses; prevent hypothermia
resources: Pelvic binder (or sheet), scoop, collar, IV x2, warm NS, blankets. UVMMC (Level 1) ~20 min ground; air medical ETA ~20 min + LZ time
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to Route 116 in Hinesburg near Silver St for a single-vehicle rollover. One patient, conscious. Fire is en route. Time out 1735.

scene.location: Rural 2-lane, ~20 min from UVMMC, dusk, 28 F, wet leaves. Car upright in ditch after 1 roll, roof crushed ~14 in at driver side.
scene.setup: Pt still in driver seat, restrained, airbags deployed. Driver door removed by FD.
scene.moulage: Seatbelt abrasion L shoulder to R hip, glass in hair, pale.
scene.roles: Pt actor; FD officer (asks "want us to backboard her?"); PD.

patient.name: Megan Ouellette
patient.on_arrival: Restrained in seat, pale, anxious, moaning, guarding pelvis, answers questions.

SAMPLE: Pelvic/groin pain, low abd pain, "cold", thirsty
Swerved for deer, went off road, rolled once. Belted. No LOC

primary: RR 24, equal, seatbelt abrasion; clear bilat
Radial weak, rapid. Pale, cool, clammy. **Shock**
GCS 15 initially, anxious. Moves all 4, pain w/ legs
Pelvic instability on single gentle compression; perineal bruising. Cold - cover
**HIGH**: hemorrhagic shock, pelvic fx. Load and go
secondary: Belt abrasion, no crepitus, equal sounds
Lower abd tender, belt sign below umbilicus
R leg slightly shortened, ext rotated; distal pulses weak equal
Low back pain; check during scoop

vitals.other: Radial palpable. Pain better after binder

vitals.trigger: IF no binder or scene > 15 min

vitals.other: BP up briefly, then drops 10 min later (re-bleed, dilution, hypothermia)
Titrated 250 mL boluses to radial pulse / mentation

flow.give: Read dispatch. FD: "Car's stable, door's off." Give mechanism (roof intrusion 14 in).
expected: Early TRAUMA ALERT plan; minimize scene time

flow.give: Stage **A**. Pelvic exam: instability with ONE gentle compression.
FD officer: "Want us to log-roll her onto a board?"

branches.if: Binder at trochanters + scoop/ rapid extrication

expected: Scoop, not log-roll; legs bound together

expected.text: Warm blankets, heat on in rig

flow.give: Ask CC: "Where are we going and how?" (UVMMC 20 min ground; air ETA 20 min + LZ; intercept ETA 15 min)

branches.then: flight arrives after ground would reach UVMMC; debrief when air helps

expected: Intercept only en route, no delay

branches.then: Stage **C** values; expect 250 mL boluses to radial pulse/mentation, MD after 1 L, update UVMMC
expect IO (6.4) or go with one line; no added scene/delay

expected: IV x2 large bore, warm NS

expected.text: 250 mL boluses to radial pulse/mentation, SBP ~90
Med Direction after 1 L; reassess q5

expected: MIST report: mechanism, injuries, signs, tx

critical: Log-roll onto long board with suspected pelvic fx
Hemorrhagic shock not recognized/no TRAUMA ALERT
differentials: Unstable pelvis, groin pain, shock, leg shortened
debrief: Which 4.9 criteria made this a Level 1 patient?
Why scoop instead of log-roll for pelvic fx?
Why limit fluids? What's your endpoint?
Why ground over air here? When would air make sense?
How did you use the fire department?

crew_card.dispatch: Route 116, Hinesburg, near Silver St. Single-vehicle rollover. 1 pt, conscious. FD en route. 28 F, dusk, wet road.
crew_card.on_arrival: Sedan upright in ditch, roof crushed on driver side, airbags out. Woman in driver seat, belted, moaning, pale. FD stabilizing car.

actor_card.Act: Pale, shivering, moan. Hold your hips. Answer clearly at first.
actor_card.Pelvis touched: Yell in pain. If touched again, scream louder and cry.
actor_card.If log-rolled: Scream 10/10, then get confused ("where am I?").
actor_card.Ask: "Is my car totaled? Can someone call my husband?"

show_cards.title: VEHICLE
show_cards.body:
Roof intrusion driver side ~14 in.
Airbags deployed. Belt worn.
Windshield starred passenger side.

show_cards.title: PELVIS / LEGS
show_cards.body:
Pelvis shifts with gentle pressure.
Bruising perineum.
R leg 2 cm shorter, rotated out.

show_cards.title: ABDOMEN
show_cards.body:
Seatbelt bruise across lower abdomen.
Tender below navel. Not distended (yet).

moulage_tags.text: Seatbelt bruise L shoulder to R hip
Shifts with gentle pressure; severe pain
moulage_tags.cue: Allow ONE gentle compression; scream if repeated

moulage_tags.text: Pulses weak but equal; can feel touch
